hypothesis: Something in Rounds 1-43 or in the repository was left over: a dropped lead, a closure wider than its measurement, an instrument or loader defect, an unexamined input, or a premise every lane shares.
threshold: FOUND-ERROR / NO-ERROR-FOUND per item (doctrine R6); every item cited to file and line
result: FOUND-ERROR, many. Thirteen partition readers plus coordinator re-verification. Headline items: the oracle failed a correct continuous key (fixed); corpus.parse() flagged the book head and tail as solved and two Round 26 lanes were aimed mid-book (fixed); the plaintext is spelled one rune per letter by the cleartext word lengths; natural-language running keys are excluded key-free by monogram flatness; the 'repeated 7-gram' is a mis-recorded 6-rune two-word repeat; pages 28/42 are position-wise related; four finite high-prior key spaces were never swept at power; seven shared decoder premises are unrepresented. See AUDIT.md sections 1-6.
coverage: All round folders 10-43, the campaign-era folders, research/ Rounds 1-9, corpus/, the ledger, ceiling, pickup and oracle layers. Reader claims marked [R] in AUDIT.md were not independently re-run.
not_covered: Image-level checks (the page renders are gitignored and absent from the audit checkout); any network source; the stale ledger rows listed in AUDIT.md section 6 were not edited.
reopens_if: n/a (audit; each item carries its own)

result.verdict: REFUTED as the default: the histogram fits letter-wise English (THE = three runes) and not the solved-page spelling. The instrument recovers letter-wise plants, so no sweep negative is voided.

coverage: 61 committed English texts (data/keys), middle 70 % of each file; two spellings; LP2's 2,928 words. Readers B and I add the solved pages (two-rune words 24.3 % vs 15.9 %, z = 4.9) and 21,698 windows.
not_covered: A non-English or article-free register that happens to match; partial unfolding (TH only) versus full letter-wise is not separated; pf_v4_12 head-screen power for letter-wise text is a reader probe (0.975-0.983), not a lane result.

hypothesis: The LP2 key is a natural-language running key (any text, any offset, either sign, any skip relation) over an English plaintext.
threshold: family excluded if the predicted and planted monogram chi-square of such a ciphertext exceeds the observed value by more than 10x at N = 12,956 (fixed before the plants were run)
control_detail: 12 planted running-key ciphertexts (English on English, both spellings, both signs, anti-repeat key-skip filter on): monogram chi2 515 to 914; LP2 observed 26.4 on 28 df.

result.key_marginal_bound: the key's own monogram distribution must be uniform to within about a 15 % English admixture
result.verdict: NEGATIVE at the family level, key-free. Discharges R12-C2, the remainder of R26-B-KEYTEXT-RUNNINGKEY-SKIPAWARE and the Round 42 10-keytext refetch without a decode.

coverage: Any additive combination of an English plaintext with a key whose symbols are natural-language letters used one per rune, at any offset, with or without the anti-repeat filter.
not_covered: Keys derived from a text by hashing or any transform that flattens the monogram distribution; a text key over a non-language plaintext; non-additive combination.
null: analytic (convolution of two measured English distributions) plus 12 plants
reopens_if: the canonical ciphertext's monogram distribution is shown to be mis-transcribed at the 20x level (it is not)

hypothesis: The repeated n-gram at page 27 offset 28 and page 54 offset 70 is a chance event at the 13 % level (ARMADA-20-FINDINGS) / a 7-gram at 0.5 % (round43 F3).
threshold: descriptive; three expectations reported so the choice of statistic is visible

the_repeat.translit: D J U - B E I

site_2.note: the last six runes of the unsolved stream

the_repeat.seventh_rune: site 1 is followed by AE; site 2 is followed by the first rune of the SOLVED page AN END, also AE (a 1-in-29 coincidence across a cipher boundary, which is how a 13,041-rune count made it a '7-gram')

coverage: All repeated n-grams, n >= 5, in the 12,956-rune stream; word-aware nulls with the cleartext skeleton fixed.
not_covered: Why it is there. No reset at a visible boundary puts the two sites at one key position; the page images of both sites were not inspected (renders absent from the audit checkout).
reopens_if: n/a (measurement); use it as a free constraint on any generator hypothesis that reaches both sites

hypothesis: The LP2 key is periodic (any period from 2 to about 12,000), with or without key-consuming rejections.
threshold: descriptive: z of the lag-L coincidence count for every L, rigid, and a Poisson-smeared matched filter for key-consuming skips; no threshold fixed in advance
positive_control: reader plants only (unregistered): drift-aware detectors recovered periods up to about 1,000-1,500 (readers A1, B, F); the coordinator's own scan carries no plant

result.verdict: Flat at every lag, rigid and drift-smeared. With the readers' plants this is a measured negative for periods up to about 1,000-1,500 under key-skip and for any period under a non-consuming filter; it is unpowered above that under key-skip.

not_covered: A pre-registered lane with its own plant; periods above about 1,500 under key-consuming skips; non-English plaintext with low coincidence rate.

hypothesis: A correct key would be recognised by the instrument of record whatever the combiner constant, reflection, stream start, key stall, rejection style or plaintext numbering.
threshold: per premise: plant the correct key through pf_v4_12 + beam_v3 and read the score
positive_control: reader probes (unregistered) hand the instrument a correct key and get noise for: C=P+K+1, Beaufort, Atbash-then-add, key burned at word boundaries, deletion-type avoidance under keyskip1/2
result: OPEN. Seven shared premises are unrepresented (AUDIT.md 1.7). Proposed remedy: a language-model-free 'blind' adjudicator, possible because a key-skip at (i, j) is admissible only if K[j+1]-K[j] = C[i]-C[i-1], so the key can be tracked without a language model and paths scored by index of coincidence, which is invariant to language, orthography, plaintext numbering, a combiner constant, Atbash and Beaufort. Feasibility measured on plants (blind_adjudicator_poc.py): at L=120, 480/480 plants above the maximum of 400 wrong keys (null IoC x29 1.14 +- 0.06, max 1.41; plant minimum 1.43), across English letter-wise, English multigraph and Latin, as written / randomly relabelled / +7 constant / Beaufort.
not_covered: everything; this row exists so the premises are queryable

hypothesis: The enumerable high-prior seed spaces have been swept at power: the 2012-2014 clock-second band for glibc, Perl and PHP; Perl rand's whole 2^32; the whole bash 4.2 state cycle; TeX's default seeds.
result: NEVER RUN at power. Clock seconds: only bash 3.2 and Py2.7 integer seeds cover every second under the repaired instrument (Round 8's per-second sweep was a rigid 48-rune English kernel). Perl: the only generator with signed first-party evidence (round19/C3 section 2c'), family exactly 2^32, about 25k seeds decoded, the one prior-dense run mis-targeted (R44-A0-LOADER-CORPUS-PARSE). bash 4.2: the swept 'full orbit' is 3.6 % of the single 2,147,483,646-state LP64 cycle (ILP32 cycle 343,896), and seed = offset on that cycle (round19/G1). TeX pgf: 8,627 default seeds, pilot only. Two server timestamps (1396427599, 1389478032) recorded by round43/F5b are absent from the seed prior.
